findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket inside of the kitchen area contained bleach, detergent, and degreaser. Discussed with the PIC that sanitizer solutions should only include bleach and water. The solution was remade and tested at 100ppm (CL) to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following facility items in need of cleaning/repair:

1. The ceiling around the lighting in the kitchen has exposed drywall. Ensure these areas are painted or paneled to avoid moisture accumulation

2. The hood system is in need of cleaning

Ensure these items are resolved prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspector observed no allergen certification present at the facility. Ensure the CFPM has an allergen certificate prior to the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 4 items to not be date-marked. The items were marinara sauce cups, sliced American cheese, raw beef patties, and cut tomatoes. Discussed with PIC and PIC added date marks to all items without them. Ensure all items are date marked within 24 hours of opening or preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a bowl of shrimp in water in the standing cooler in the back of the kitchen. Discussed proper cooling methods with PIC. Ensure that frozen foods are thawed under refrigeration, or in running cool water at 70F or below. Food must not be thawed in standing water. PIC drained the water from the bowl and continued thawing shrimp under refrigeration.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed 4 physical facilities in need of maintenance.

-The first place was the seal on the wall behind the fryers. The seal between NUDO boards is pulling from the wall. Ensure that it is repaired or replaced to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface.

-A light has recently been replaced in the kitchen, ensure the ceiling around the light is repainted to cover the drywall above. Drywall is absorbent, and surfaces in the kitchen must be nonabsorbent.

-There was an accumulation of flour and dust on dry storage shelves as well as the vent above them. Ensure these areas are cleared of debris, and cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean. Along with this, the floor under the shelves held some food debris. Ensure this area is swept regularly to prevent the build-up of debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Multiple employees were observed to wash their hands and then turn off the faucet without a barrier. It is important that a barrier is used when washing your hands to avoid recontamination to your hands. CORRECTED- The staff was educated and the issue was corrected on site. 

(A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: There was a cutting board observed to be stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. A cutting board is a food contact surface and the faucet causes contamination to the surface. CORRECTED- The cutting board was moved and washed during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch. 

 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: There is observed to be a leak in the triple sink faucet. Ensure that this leak is repaired and maintained in good repair. 

A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Containers in the back by the freezer containing lids were observed to have food residue on the lids and in the containers.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure utensils and lids are covered or protected from food splash to prevent contamination.

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Hood baffles were observed to have an accumulation of grease and dust.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure baffles are cleaned in between service dates.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Mop was observed to be stored with the mop head down on the floor.  Ensure mop is stored in a way to allow air-drying of the mop. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Caulking around the hand sink in the bar needs to be replaced.  The caulking is coming away from the wall creating a non easily cleanable space.  Ensure the caulk is replaced to create a smooth, easily cleanable, non absorbent surface.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Vents in the kitchen and dry storage area were observed to contain dust and mold.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure vents are cleaned regularly to prevent mold and dust accumulation.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Hand washing sink in kitchen did not have paper towels available.  Hand washing sink in bar did not have soap or paper towels available.  These items are to be readily available to employees. During the inspection, PIC restocked the paper towels at each sink and stocked hand soap at the bar sink. Ensure hand washing sinks are stocked with soap and paper towels at all times.  

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Hoods above the fryers were observed to contain build-up of grease and dust debris.  PIC states he does not have a contract with a hood cleaning company, but does have Mike Bearden clean the hood as needed.  The facility is not open to the public and is used mainly as a catering company.  Grease and dust build-up on baffles can cause contamination of foods being prepared.  PIC is advised to contact Mike Bearden to have hood cleaned as soon as possible. A follow-up is being scheduled for 9/12/2022. A discussion with the PIC has taken place and if the facility is unable to obtain hood cleaning by this date, then the PIC will inform the inspector. The hoods are in desperate need of being cleaned and need to be done ASAP if the 3 day follow-up is to soon. This item will be reevaluated when inspector speaks with PIC before the 3 day follow-up.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Kitchen shelving was observed to contain a build-up of dust and food debris.  Food contact surfaces shall be protected from cross contamination during storage.  Ensure shelving is cleaned frequently to avoid build up of dust and food debris.

Ceiling vents in kitchen were observed to contain dust and mold.  Dust and mold build-up could cause contamination of foods.  Ensure vents and ceiling around are frequently cleaned to prevent contamination.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Mop was observed to be stored in the mop bucket with soiled water.  Ensure mop is stored in a way to allow air-drying of the mop. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under ¶¶ 3-301.11(B) and (E). 
 Observed employee use beverage cup to scoop ice out of ice container. Discussed with employee and PIC. Ensure ice scoop is used to place ice in beverages to prevent cross contamination of hands and ice.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). 

Observed several proteins in the glass coolers in kitchen out of order on shelving, thus exposing them to cross contamination. Observed Raw chicken, pork and beef product stored above fish product in the cooler. Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff reference the posted storage order sheet on door when putting product away. Items with the highest internal cooking temperatures (poultry) must be on the bottom, followed by ground meat products, then whole chops/steaks, then fish, then RTE foods at the very top. COS- Inspector and PIC shifted product to proper storage order.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Exhaust hood above the grill/fryer areas observed with accumulated dust and grease debris. Hood hasn’t been serviced since before last routine inspection. See that SteamPower is contacted for a cleaning by next routine. Ensure hood system is cleaned as frequently as needed to prevent accumulation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only. 

Observed employee utilize the bar triple sink to wash hands. COS- Discussed with PIC and employee. Staff should only be washing hands in a designated hand sink to prevent cross contamination between warewashing facilities and hands. Ensure staff are trained on proper handwashing technique, when to wash, and where to wash on a periodic basis.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Observed container of Tilapia in vacuum packaging to be thawing in the glass refrigerator. Discussed with PIC. Ensure foods stored in reduced-oxygen-packaging have the packaging sliced before thawing per thawing instructions on the package. Ensure staff continue this practice as it prevents anaerobic bacteria from thriving while thawing. COS- PIC sliced packaging of thawing fish.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

There is about 8” circular hole in ceiling directly above the dry storage area covered up with what appears to be cardboard. Ensure the wall is patched with drywall and sealed to prevent potential contamination and/or pest entry to the dry storage area.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. 

Entire restaurant remodeled after a fire, and hand sinks lacked signage notifying employees to wash hands. Inspector provided signs to cover all hand sinks.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P) Shell eggs are stored above RTE foods in vertical stainless steel cooler. Ensure shell eggs are stored on lower level of cooler to prevent accidental cross contamination. Eggs moved during inspection.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Only chlorine test strips are available in facility, but quat is also a sanitizing solution used in facility (at bar sink). Ensure test kits are available for all sanitizing agents utilized within facility. Contact inspector by follow up date when test strips have been purchased.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Grease and debris buildup in grooves of glass coolers (doorframe) in fridge as well as underneath the cooler. Ensure these items are cleaned from built up grease deposits and are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent accumulation.

findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Ensure hand sinks in men's and women's restrooms are caulked to the wall to prevent moisture from getting behind the sink and accumulating. Correct by next routine inspection.
